item.title: Iran can’t have nuclear weapons but North Korea can? There’s logic here.
item.description: There’s real logic beneath Trump’s split nuclear strategy. Iran and North Korea present very different nonproliferation problems.

item.title: There’s Real Logic Beneath Trump’s Split Nuclear Strategy
item.description: As President Trump moves in opposite directions on Iran and North Korea’s nuclear programs, CSIS's Victor Cha unpacks the split nuclear strategy in the Washington Post.

item.title: The Emperor’s Wardrobe Malfunction
item.description: In this week’s column, Bill Reinsch argues that countries have begun adapting to the Trump administration’s trade policy by pursuing nonbinding agreements that offer immediate appeasement but provide limited enforceability.

item.title: As Tokyo and Manila Talk Boundaries, Beijing Breaks Them
item.description: How long will China’s patrols and surveys east of Taiwan continue?

item.title: States Weekly: August 19, 2026
item.description: This edition of States Weekly covers August 19, 2026.

item.title: Mapping Iranian Cyberattacks on U.S. Water Systems
item.description: Recent Iranian cyberattacks on U.S. water systems were months in the making. These charts combine press reporting and CSIS expert analysis to provide a clearer picture of the attacks and their impact on the U.S. water sector.

item.title: Beyond Line of Sight: How Part 108 Could Transform Commercial Drones
item.description: The FAA’s proposed Part 108 rule could unlock routine beyond-visual-line-of-sight drone operations, transforming emergency response, infrastructure inspection, and logistics. But getting the safety architecture right will determine whether the United States leads the next era of autonomous aviation.

item.title: Tracking FY 2027 Defense Appropriations, Reconciliation, and the Supplemental Request
item.description: As the October 1 start of the fiscal year (FY) approaches, Congress has yet to enact defense funding for FY 2027. Seamus Daniels outlines the current status of legislation in response to the Trump administration’s $1.5 trillion defense budget request.

item.title: The Implications of Japan’s New National Intelligence Bureau
item.description: Japan’s new National Intelligence Bureau is an important early step in Japanese intelligence reform and creates opportunities for deeper cooperation with the United States and other partners.

item.title: Are SBIR “Mills” Truly a Problem?
item.description: The Small Business Innovation Research Program has faced suggestions that a small number of “mills” receive a disproportionate share of awards while underperforming on innovation and commercialization metrics. An analysis of grant recipient data suggests this pattern reflects a division between specialized defense research contractors and dual-use venture-backed companies.
